title: The Shunammite (2 Kings 4:8–37)
hookLine: a woman builds the prophet a room and asks nothing: "I dwell among mine own people"
last: AN OLD CLOAK LYING ON THE GROUND.

lines: A SMALL ROOM ON THE ROOF.
A BED, A TABLE, A STOOL, A LAMP.
cards: A bed, a table, a stool and a lamp. The text lists them item by item. A woman in Shunem, called a great woman, has been inviting the traveling prophet Elisha to eat whenever he passes through.

Then she goes further. She tells her husband: this is a holy man of God who keeps passing by. Let's build him a small room on the roof, with a bed, a table, a stool and a lamp, so he has a place to rest.

teach.h: WHAT CAN BE DONE FOR THEE?
teach.b: One day, resting in that room, Elisha wants to repay her. He sends his servant Gehazi with an offer: you've taken all this trouble for us; what can be done for you?
Shall we speak for you to the king, or to the captain of the army? It's a real offer; a prophet's word in the right ear could open doors.

teach.h: I DWELL AMONG MINE OWN PEOPLE.
teach.b: Her answer is quiet and complete: "I dwell among mine own people." Her hospitality wasn't an investment. Elisha doesn't let it go.
Gehazi points out that she has no son, and her husband is old. So Elisha tells her: about this season next year, you will hold a son.

teach.h: DO NOT LIE TO THY HANDMAID.
teach.b: Her reply is startling: no, my lord, do not lie to your handmaid. She had never asked for it. And the son is born.
When the child has grown, he goes out to his father in the field and cries, my head, my head. He is carried to his mother, and dies on her lap.

She lays him on the prophet's bed in the little room, shuts the door, and rides straight to find Elisha. Asked on the way whether all is well, she says only: it is well. Then at Elisha's feet the grief pours out.
Elisha comes, prays, stretches himself over the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes. And look where the miracle happens: in the room she built for a stranger.
The space she made out of kindness, asking nothing, became the place where her son was given back to her.

how: Jews read the story of the Shunammite as a haftarah alongside the Torah reading of Abraham's welcome to his guests, and welcoming guests, hachnasat orchim, is honored as a mitzvah.

games.q: you've built a room for a traveling prophet. he offers to put in a word for you with the king. what do you say?
o: yes, a word at court would help.
no thanks: I dwell among my own people.
ask for money for the room.
games.why: she says, I dwell among mine own people. she didn't make room to get something back.

practice: Look around at the spaces you have, a spare chair, a corner of a table, and think of someone who passes through your life a little tired: a new coworker, a neighbor living alone, a friend who's been quiet.
Picture what the Shunammite's small room would look like for them, a plate, a chair, set out expecting nothing back.

wordCard.voice: The Shunammite. The woman of Shunem who built a small room for a traveling prophet and, offered a favor at court, said she dwelt among her own people. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: among my people I dwell, her answer in 2 Kings 4:13.

carryVoice: Your line: I dwell among my people. She gave a room and asked for nothing. Until tomorrow.
